articles.summary: Nearly every household seems to own an air fryer these days. Consumers are increasingly looking for healthier food options while still expecting the golden appearance, crispy bite, and satisfying taste traditionally associated with fried foods. For food producers, this raises an important question: how do you deliver healthier, crispy, and succulent snack foods on an industrial scale without compromising on quality, consistency, or throughput?
articles.title: JBT Marel industrial air frying solution

articles.summary: For deboning and trimming turkey breast fillets, JBT Marel has developed the StreamLine for turkeys. It is the right choice for processing plants that cannot automate due to excessive flock variation, exceptional sizes or too many different products. In markets where labor is incentive‑driven, or where manual labor is simply preferred over automation, StreamLine is the ideal answer.
articles.title: StreamLine for turkeys

articles.summary: When a poultry processor has tenderloins available in bulk batches or in a random flow, but the retail customer requires fixed weight or fixed count trays, the first challenge is to separate the products into individual pieces. This process, called singulation, is where the SingleFeed plays a crucial role by taking over a labor-intensive manual task that would otherwise require at least two operators. SingleFeed automatically singulates bulk products, preparing them for further in-line processing.
articles.title: SingleFeed for successful singulation

articles.summary: At various points in the post deboning process, operators reinsert products onto the conveyor belt at random after completing their manual tasks. This creates a risk of product overlap when singulated products are required. With JBT Marel OneFlow, suitable for use with AMF-i, trimming stations and SensorX, the product flow on the belt can be kept consistent. It ensures individual processing downstream and minimizes rejects. Not in the least, OneFlow has considerable ergonomical advantages for the operators.
articles.title: OneFlow reinserts products with the right timing

The line is now available for customer demonstrations and product trials, including salad wash line and wash and dry line applications.
articles.title: See the salad and vegetable processing line in action at the Lakeland Customer Innovation Center

articles.summary: New regulations are reshaping how Norway's seafood industry receives wild-caught fish. From January 1, 2027, operators receiving wild-caught pelagic fish must have automatic scales and automatic weighing system (AWS) in place. Wild-caught whitefish operators face the same requirement one year later, from January 1, 2028.
articles.title: AXIN Solution built to meet Norwegian weighing compliance deadlines
